findings.summary: allowed_bots allowlist is broader than the stated "our own App only" intent: it also admits the plain, non-bot-suffixed username "yorkie-agent", not just the App's actual bot identity "yorkie-agent[bot]".
findings.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` is meant to admit only the project's own GitHub App bot so claude-code-action will act on the workflow_run triggered by the agent's own push. Every push in this pipeline is authenticated via `actions/create-github-app-token` (confirmed: agent-iterate-ci.yml:57, agent-review-panel.yml:371-374, agent-implement.yml:74, agent-review-reply.yml:85 are the only push-credential mints in the repo), whose resulting actor always renders as `<slug>[bot]` — i.e. `yorkie-agent[bot]`. The second entry, plain `yorkie-agent` (no `[bot]` suffix), does not correspond to any actor this pipeline itself produces, so it is either dead weight or — if GitHub ever attributes a workflow_run actor as the bare account name (or an attacker registers/controls a GitHub account literally named `yorkie-agent`) — it widens the allowlist the comment explicitly says should admit 'ONLY our own App'. Since the guarded action is claude-code-action running with a GitHub App token that has `contents: write` and executes autonomous branch code, an allowlist entry that isn't cryptographically tied to the App's identity is a real (if narrow, since the job is additionally gated on head_repository==base repo and the `agent/` branch prefix, both of which still require some form of push access) widening of the authorization boundary versus the comment's stated goal of a same-App-only allowlist.

verdict.reason: Verified directly: the `stalled` job's if-condition (agent-review-panel.yml:456-460) only checks `needs.<job>.result == 'failure'` for deps/review-panel/promote/fix, with no disjunct for `'cancelled'`. The `fix` job (line 296) has `timeout-minutes: 45` and runs a claude-code-action step with `--max-turns 40` against an opus model (lines 404-432), which can plausibly exceed 45 minutes. Per GitHub Actions semantics, a job that hits its `timeout-minutes` is cancelled by the runner and its `needs.<job>.result` is reported as `'cancelled'`, not `'failure'` — so this scenario would not satisfy any of the four disjuncts and `stalled` would not fire, silently leaving the PR blocked. I grepped the entire `.github/workflows/` directory for the string `cancelled` and found zero matches in any workflow file, and read the full `stalled` job (lines 448-485) with no fallback catch-all (e.g., no `!success()`/`contains(needs.*.result,...)` pattern) that would otherwise cover a cancelled conclusion. I also checked the other workflow files (agent-iterate-ci.yml, agent-implement.yml, etc.) for any independent stall/timeout-watcher mechanism and found none relevant to this fix job. No counterexample exists in this repository.
